numerical_failure.observed_behavior: SparseArray.take(indices, allow_fill=True) promotes the subtype via type-based np.result_type(dtype, type(fill_value)) whenever a taken position lands on a gap or a -1 index, so an identity take [0, 1, 2] does not round-trip: Sparse[int8, 0] becomes Sparse[int64, 0]; Sparse[uint64, 0] becomes Sparse[float64, 0] rounding values above 2**53; Sparse[datetime64[ns], Timestamp(...)] becomes Sparse[object] holding raw integers; Sparse[datetime64[s], Timestamp(...)] becomes Sparse[datetime64[us]]; Sparse[datetime64[ns]] with no gaps raises DTypePromotionError.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The result dtype should be kept when the subtype already holds the fill value (gaps need no promotion, and a -1 fill should follow the value rather than its type), so the identity take round-trips without widening or precision loss; datetimelike sparse columns should keep their unit (e.g. Sparse[M8[s]] should not be widened to nanoseconds).
trigger_conditions: a taken position lands on a gap (sparse fill position) or on a -1 index
subtype is int8, uint64, datetime64[ns] or datetime64[s] with a fill value, or datetime64[ns] with no gaps
reached in practice via Series.reindex, DataFrame.reindex, .loc[list], alignment and GroupBy.first/last
